```{python}
#| label: cargar-resumen
from pathlib import Path
import sys

ROOT = Path.cwd().parent if Path.cwd().name == "docs" else Path.cwd()
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
from report_helpers import read_result, kpis, number, share, show_table, ci

grd_sources = read_result("grd_source_inventory.csv")
rem_quality = read_result("rem_quality.csv")
epi_quality = read_result("grd_epi_quality.csv")
grd_summary = read_result("grd_cohort_summary.csv")
rates = read_result("grd_rates_national.csv")
trends = read_result("grd_trends_apc.csv")
sex_ratio = read_result("grd_sex_ratio.csv")
rem_rates = read_result("rem_rates_national.csv")
rem_annual = read_result("rem_annual_by_code.csv")
moran = read_result("grd_spatial_moran.csv")
cohort = grd_summary.query("era == '2021-2024' and definition == 'TEA_operacional'").iloc[0]
main = rates.loc[(rates.definition == "TEA_operacional") & (rates.role == "cualquiera") & (rates.sex == "TOTAL")]
records = main.loc[main.unit == "records"].set_index("year")
persons = main.loc[main.unit == "persons"].set_index("year")
last_year = int(records.index.max())
apc = trends.query("definition == 'TEA_operacional' and unit == 'records' and role == 'cualquiera' and sex == 'TOTAL' and period == '2021-2024'").iloc[0]
ratio = sex_ratio.query("definition == 'TEA_operacional' and unit == 'records' and role == 'cualquiera'").set_index("year")
rem_last = rem_rates.loc[(rem_rates.series == "05990022") & (rem_rates.sex == "TOTAL")].set_index("year")
rem_ingresos = rem_annual.loc[rem_annual.code == "05990022"].set_index("year").Col01
moran_main = moran.query("unit == 'records' and variable == 'sir_eb'").iloc[0]

kpis([
    (number(grd_sources.records.sum()), "GRD records read · 2019–2024"),
    (number(epi_quality.records_kept.sum()), "Records with an F84 code"),
    (number(rem_quality.records.sum()), "REM Series A rows · 2017–2024"),
    (number(cohort.patients), "Identifiers in the trajectory cohort · 2021–2024"),
])
```

## Three questions, two sources

**[GRD: hospital epidemiology and trajectories](grd.html).** Describes hospitalisations with an autism spectrum disorder (ASD) code in the public system: magnitude and trend, age-standardised population rates, sex and age, subcategories, code position, episode characteristics, co-diagnoses, readmission, regions, communes and spatial autocorrelation. It also reconstructs which hospital diagnoses precede the first observed autism record and in which position it is recorded.

**[REM: outpatient activity, screening and rehabilitation](rem.html).** Describes entries to and discharges from mental-health programmes with an autism code, their population rates, age, sex, regions, communes and facilities, screening in well-child check-ups (MCHAT and M-CHAT R/F) and rehabilitation entries, and compares both sources ecologically.

**[Methods](methods.html).** Sources, case definitions, units, denominators, standardisation, intervals, trends, spatial analysis, REM reading rules, quality controls, biases, limitations and reproducibility. It is the common reference of the two reports.

## The manuscript for The Lancet Regional Health – Americas

**[Article (version 10)](lancet.html).** Administrative recognition of autism in Chile's public health and education systems, 2019–2025: a national multi-source study. Reproduces the text with its citations, the two tables and the four panel figures of the manuscript; the plates are regenerated from `docs/lancet/` with the same scripts as the submitted version, in English and Spanish.

**[Supplementary material](lancet_supplement.html).** Extended methods (A1–A11, 23 equations), complementary results, tables S1–S9 and figures S1–S9.

**[Extended corpus](lancet_corpus.html).** The 59 plates and 132 tables of the earlier versions of the study (`lancet_americas/` pipeline, variant without Rett syndrome), so that no result is left out of the site.

## Main results

```{python}
#| label: hallazgos-principales
kpis([
    (number(records.loc[last_year, "asr"], 1), f"Hospitalisations with an ASD code per 100 000 person-years, age-standardised · {last_year} (was {number(records.asr.iloc[0], 1)} in {int(records.index.min())})"),
    (number(persons.loc[last_year, "asr"], 1), f"Hospitalised persons with an ASD code per 100 000 population · {last_year}"),
    (number(apc.apc, 1) + "%", f"Average annual percent change · 2021–2024 (95% CI: {ci(apc.apc_lo, apc.apc_hi)})"),
    (number(ratio.loc[last_year, "asr_ratio"], 2), f"Male:female rate ratio · {last_year} (was {number(ratio.asr_ratio.iloc[0], 2)} in {int(ratio.index.min())})"),
    (number(rem_last.loc[last_year, "asr"], 1), f"REM A05 entries with an autism code per 100 000 population, age-standardised · {last_year} ({number(rem_ingresos.loc[last_year])} entries)"),
    (number(moran_main.moran_i, 2), "Moran's I of the smoothed commune hospitalisation ratio (permutation p " + number(moran_main.p_sim, 3) + ")"),
    (number(share(cohort.prior_hospitalization, cohort.patients), 1) + "%", "2021–2024 cohort with observable prior hospitalisations"),
])
```

Hospitalisations and outpatient programme entries with an autism code have grown rapidly since 2021, more in females than in males, with the greatest intensity between 5 and 14 years of age and with strong territorial heterogeneity. These increases are consistent with greater detection, greater demand and coding changes in the period of Law 21.545; **they do not demonstrate an increase in the occurrence of autism**. No figure in these reports is incidence or prevalence: they are rates of hospitalisations, of hospitalised persons and of recorded programme entries.

In the 2021–2024 hospital trajectories, the first autism record almost always occurs with the code in a secondary position, and only a minority has observable prior hospitalisations. The earlier codes do not show that they were ruled out as differential diagnoses: they may be comorbidities, symptoms or independent reasons for admission.

## How the analyses are organised

```{python}
#| label: tabla-organizacion
import pandas as pd
organisation = pd.DataFrame([
    ("GRD · A1", "Universe, units and quality", "grd_epi_quality, grd_annual_positions"),
    ("GRD · A2", "Annual trend, crude and standardised rates, AAPC, seasonality, sensitivity", "grd_rates_national, grd_trends_apc, grd_epi_monthly"),
    ("GRD · A3", "Sex ratio, single year of age, age-specific rates", "grd_sex_ratio, grd_epi_age_single, grd_rates_age_specific"),
    ("GRD · A4", "F84 subcategories and code position", "grd_rates_subcodes, grd_epi_subcodes"),
    ("GRD · A5", "Admission, activity, specialty, insurance, discharge, case fatality, length of stay, severity, hospitals", "grd_epi_features, grd_epi_los_*, grd_epi_grd_weight, grd_epi_hospitals"),
    ("GRD · A6", "Readmission and multiplicity", "grd_epi_readmissions, grd_epi_multiplicity"),
    ("GRD · A7", "Co-diagnoses and principal diagnosis", "grd_epi_codiagnoses"),
    ("GRD · A8", "Regions, communes, indirect standardisation, Moran, LISA", "grd_rates_regional, grd_rates_comunal, grd_spatial_*"),
    ("GRD · B", "Trajectories: linkage, position, prior diagnoses, sequences, transitions", "grd_cohort_*, grd_first_*, grd_previous_*, grd_sequences, grd_principal_transitions"),
    ("REM", "Entries, rates, age and sex, subcategories, regions, communes, panel, screening, rehabilitation, ecological comparison", "rem_*"),
], columns=["Section", "Content", "Tables in output_files/consolidacion"])
show_table(organisation, "Report sections and the aggregate tables that feed them")
```

The seven documents run **Python** and read the aggregate tables of `output_files/consolidacion/`. Tables and figures are recalculated at render time; they contain no hand-pasted figures. The extraction from the original files runs separately, through the scripts documented in the [repository README](../README.md). The earlier reports, their HTML and their resources were kept in `others scripts/`, outside `docs`, for traceability only.

## Interpretation priorities

| Source | Already available | Next extension |
|---|---|---|
| GRD | Crude and standardised rates with intervals, trends, sex and age, subcategories, position, episode characteristics, co-diagnoses, readmission, regions, communes, Moran and LISA, cohorts and trajectories | Confirm the linkage with the producer, models adjusted for age, sex, year, contacts and hospital, incorporate deaths and emergency care, validate clinical records |
| REM | 2017–2024 series, standardised entry rates, age and sex, subcategories, regions, communes, facility panel, screening indicators by stage, rehabilitation, ecological comparison | Validate screening denominators with the manuals, incorporate Series P (population under control), review 2025–2026 |

The original data remain in the external root configured through `ASESORIAS_DATA_ROOT`. The extraction used does not incorporate REM 2025–2026: those files require reviewing integrity, coverage and comparability before extending the series.
